This segues into a funny story. A couple years ago I went for a run down my town's trainrail-turned-exercise-trail. Being an old train line it naturally went through the 'neglected' parts of town. Unfortunately the trail at the time was woefully lacking water fountains so I had to duck into a liquor store in hopes of finding Gatorade or equivalent. After finding hoped for nourishment I was standing outside the store when I was approached by one of the store's patrons. I kid you not, this was the conversation (bear in mind it was around 10am and I had my phone in one of those arm strap thingies).

Patron: that's a cool holder for your phone. Where did you get it? Me: Amazon Patron: ...where's that? Me: ...Amazon.com...on the Web Patron: ...where's that? Me: On the internet.... Patron: Never heard of it... Me: Well, I need to get back to my run. Hope you have a nice day...

Dude couldn't have been older that 45.

So for any responders remember there are literally people who have not heard of Amazon.

Sure, you write "The object of the megathreads is to have as much information as possible in one place, where people can go to research the items."

If the goal is to have all information in one place, I don't understand the value in separate threads for authentics and clones, or breaking tanks into three categories.

They're broken down into categories as they are so people coming into it can find the relevant information easily. For instance, if someone wants to learn if they should purchase a Herakles over a Subtank, they don't want to have to wade through reviews for the Nautilus or EVOD II.

Separating authentics from clones is for a similar reason - if you want to sort by new to see the newest authentic tanks, you don't want to have to sort through the flood of newly released clones.
